1	// Wire contract between the QEMU TCG plugin and vsim. Both sides write/read
2	// `struct hybrid_state_v1` byte-for-byte through a shared file.
3	//
4	// Stability: never repurpose offsets within a published version. Add new
5	// fields by consuming bytes from `reserved`, or by introducing v2 alongside.
6	//
7	// Endianness: multi-byte fields are little-endian (native on RV64 + x86-64
8	// host). The format is not endian-portable; cross-endian use would need an
9	// explicit byte-swap path.
10	//
11	// C and C++ both compile this header.
12	
13	#ifndef HYBRID_STATE_ABI_H
14	#define HYBRID_STATE_ABI_H
15	
16	#include <stdint.h>
17	#include <stddef.h>
18	
19	#ifdef __cplusplus
20	extern "C" {
21	#endif
22	
23	#define HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC   0x42594841u  // 'AHYB' little-endian
24	// Version 3 (Andes F0): append struct hybrid_andes_csr after mmisc_ctl, which
25	// grows the struct. Version 2 (L11) widened vreg[] to 128 bytes/register.
26	// Readers reject older files loudly (all three consumers check magic + version
27	// + size) instead of mis-parsing them.
28	#define HYBRID_STATE_VERSION 3u
29	
30	#define HYBRID_FLAG_RV64  (1u << 0)
31	#define HYBRID_FLAG_FP    (1u << 1)
32	#define HYBRID_FLAG_V     (1u << 2)
33	// v3: the struct hybrid_andes_csr block carries live values (the producer ran
34	// on an Andes core that implements at least one of those CSRs). Clear means the
35	// block is all-zero and consumers skip restore/re-read/compare of it.
36	#define HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES (1u << 3)
37	
38	// VLEN upper bound, in bytes: 128 covers the supported engine range
39	// VLEN 128..1024 (L11; also QEMU's RV_VLEN_MAX). This is the wire-format
40	// span per vector register; the LIVE width is the runtime `vlenb` field
41	// below, so one struct layout serves every engine config and the legs
42	// never disagree on offsets. A producer whose vlenb exceeds this ceiling
43	// must refuse to drain (see hybrid_v_drain_policy) rather than truncate.
44	#define HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX 128
45	
46	// L26: bytes reserved for the V-register transport scratch page -- 32 vector
47	// registers at the wire-format span. The driver maps this many bytes ABOVE
48	// the program's --mem-size (so the scratch sits past the program's RAM), and
49	// vsim's v_scratch_gpa() / kVScratchBytes use the same count. Shared here so
50	// the producer (driver mmap sizing) and consumer (vsim sweep) never disagree.
51	#define HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES (32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX)
52	
53	// 64 PMP entries; pmpcfg slots reserved at 16 so the layout works for both
54	// RV64 (8 entries/CSR) and a future RV32 (4 entries/CSR) packing.
55	#define HYBRID_PMP_CFG_NUM  16
56	#define HYBRID_PMP_ADDR_NUM 64
57	
58	// v3 Andes CSR block. PMA is 16 entries: pmacfg packs them at one byte each, so
59	// on RV64 only the even-numbered cfg CSRs exist -- 16 entries live in pmacfg0
60	// (0xBC0) + pmacfg2 (0xBC2), hence 2 cfg slots; 16 pmaaddr (0xBD0..0xBDF).
61	#define HYBRID_PMA_CFG_NUM  2
62	#define HYBRID_PMA_ADDR_NUM 16
63	#define HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR   0xBC0
64	#define HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR  0xBD0
65	
66	// Single source of truth for the SCALAR Andes CSRs transported in v3: X(field,
67	// csr_addr, gdb_name). Every consumer (QEMU plugin drain, ResumeDriver restore,
68	// StateDrain re-read, driver state_diff verify) iterates this list, so adding a
69	// CSR is one line here -- no consumer edits drift out of sync. PMA (arrays) is
70	// transported separately, mirroring the existing PMP loops. Each field is a
71	// 64-bit CSR value; 0 means the producing engine did not implement it (a
72	// tolerant no-op on restore). Order fixes the struct layout -- append only.
73	#define HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)            \
74	  X(mxstatus,       0x7C4, "mxstatus")      \
75	  X(mpft_ctl,       0x7C5, "mpft_ctl")      \
76	  X(mclk_ctl,       0x7DF, "mclk_ctl")      \
77	  X(milmb,          0x7C0, "milmb")         \
78	  X(mdlmb,          0x7C1, "mdlmb")         \
79	  X(mecc_code,      0x7C2, "mecc_code")     \
80	  X(mhsp_ctl,       0x7C6, "mhsp_ctl")      \
81	  X(msp_bound,      0x7C7, "msp_bound")     \
82	  X(msp_base,       0x7C8, "msp_base")      \
83	  X(mcountermask_m, 0x7D1, "mcountermask_m")\
84	  X(uitb,           0x800, "uitb")          \
85	  X(jvt,            0x017, "jvt")           \
86	  X(ucode,          0x801, "ucode")
87	
88	// The Andes V5 machine/user CSRs a bare-metal Andes core sets up before the ROI
89	// (boot-static memory system + extension config) plus the DSP overflow flag.
90	// Restored at resume, re-read at drain, and verified -- live only when
91	// HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES is set. 13 scalar fields (above) + PMA = 31 * uint64_t.
92	struct hybrid_andes_csr {
93	#define HYBRID_ANDES_FIELD(field, addr, name) uint64_t field;
94	  HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(HYBRID_ANDES_FIELD)
95	#undef HYBRID_ANDES_FIELD
96	  uint64_t pmacfg[HYBRID_PMA_CFG_NUM];
97	  uint64_t pmaaddr[HYBRID_PMA_ADDR_NUM];
98	};
99	
100	// All fields are naturally 8-byte aligned, so __attribute__((packed)) is
101	// unnecessary and would force unaligned access codegen. Layout is locked by
102	// the static_asserts in state_abi_check.h.
103	struct hybrid_state_v1 {
104	  uint32_t magic;
105	  uint32_t version;
106	  uint32_t flags;
107	  uint32_t hart_id;
108	  uint64_t pc;
109	  uint64_t priv;  // 0=U, 1=S, 3=M
110	
111	  uint64_t gpr[32];
112	  uint64_t fpr[32];
113	
114	  uint64_t mstatus;
115	  uint64_t mepc;
116	  uint64_t mtvec;
117	  uint64_t mcause;
118	  uint64_t mtval;
119	  uint64_t mscratch;
120	  uint64_t medeleg;
121	  uint64_t mideleg;
122	  uint64_t mip;
123	  uint64_t mie;
124	  uint64_t mcycle;
125	  uint64_t minstret;
126	  uint64_t satp;
127	
128	  uint64_t pmpcfg[HYBRID_PMP_CFG_NUM];
129	  uint64_t pmpaddr[HYBRID_PMP_ADDR_NUM];
130	
131	  uint64_t vstart;
132	  uint64_t vtype;
133	  uint64_t vl;
134	  uint64_t vlenb;
135	  uint8_t  vreg[32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX];
136	  uint64_t vxsat;
137	  uint64_t vxrm;
138	  uint64_t vcsr;
139	
140	  // L20: FP control/status -- frm[7:5] | fflags[4:0], live when
141	  // HYBRID_FLAG_FP is set. Drained by the plugin, restored by ResumeDriver,
142	  // re-read by StateDrain. Pre-L20 state files carry 0 here (reserved bytes
143	  // are written as zero), which reads back as the reset value (RNE, no
144	  // flags) -- exactly the old behavior, so no version bump.
145	  uint64_t fcsr;
146	
147	  // Andes machine-setup CSRs: mcache_ctl (0x7CA) enables the L1 I/D caches,
148	  // mmisc_ctl (0x7D0) holds misc machine config. crt0 writes them once at
149	  // boot; transporting them keeps the cycle engine from resuming caches-off
150	  // (ResumeDriver has the full rationale). Drained by the plugin, restored by
151	  // ResumeDriver, but NOT re-read by StateDrain: they are boot-static and the
152	  // drained value is unused (no QEMU2 leg). Old state files carry 0 here
153	  // (reset value), which is the pre-existing behavior, so no version bump.
154	  uint64_t mcache_ctl;
155	  uint64_t mmisc_ctl;
156	
157	  // v3: Andes V5 CSR block (live when HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES). 31 * 8 = 248 bytes.
158	  struct hybrid_andes_csr andes;
159	
160	  uint8_t  reserved[64];  // zero-initialise on write; v3-compatible growth room
161	};
162	
163	#ifdef __cplusplus
164	}  // extern "C"
165	#endif
166	
167	#include "hybrid/state_abi_check.h"
168	
169	#endif  // HYBRID_STATE_ABI_H

2	// drained hybrid_state_v1 records -- the QEMU oracle's exit-boundary drain
3	// (ref) against the hybrid run's vsim drain (got).
4	//
5	// Compare policy, fixed by what vsim's drain freshly reads (state_drain.hpp
6	// drain_with_passthrough):
7	//   strict:  magic/version/flags/hart_id/priv (identity), pc, gpr[0..31],
8	//            mepc/mcause (round-trip), mscratch (L23) + mtval/mie (L24) --
9	//            round-trip M-mode CSRs restored at resume + re-read at drain;
10	//            fpr[0..31] under FLAG_FP; vstart/vtype/vl/vlenb/vxsat/vxrm/vcsr
11	//            and the vreg bytes under FLAG_V.
12	//   skipped: mstatus, mtvec, medeleg, mideleg, mip, satp, pmpcfg[], pmpaddr[].
13	//            mtvec/medeleg/mideleg/satp/PMP are passthrough on the vsim side
14	//            (copied from QEMU1's ENTRY snapshot, never re-read). mip IS
15	//            re-read but excluded here -- its pending bits are hardware-driven
16	//            and diverge between the engines' clocks. mstatus is excluded for
17	//            its dirty/impl-defined bits.
18	//   masked:  mcycle, minstret -- the engines count cycles/insns differently
19	//            by design.

content.text:
Verdict: clean on the reuse angle. No real duplication of an existing helper. Every new block reuses the right primitive and mirrors the sanctioned patterns. Details per your specific questions:

- `andes_verify_excluded` lambda (driver/state_diff.cpp:92-94) — NOT a duplication; no existing exclusion mechanism to reuse. Today `mip` and every other skipped CSR (mstatus, mtvec, medeleg, mideleg, satp, pmpcfg[], pmpaddr[]) are excluded purely by omission — there is no exclusion set, predicate, or helper anywhere in the driver (confirmed by grep; state_diff.cpp just never calls `cmp()` on them). Omission cannot express "skip 2 of 13" inside an X-macro expansion, so a local predicate is the minimal new construct. Keeping it as a file-local lambda (rather than adding a 4th "verify" column to the shared `HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST`) is correct: it keeps the verify-only concern out of the macro that the other 3 consumers share. Leave it.

- "write all CSRs in a list" helper (resume_driver.hpp:252-263) — none exists; the new code reuses `write_csr_tolerant` per entry, same as every existing scalar write. The PMA address/cfg loops intentionally mirror the existing inline PMP write loops (resume_driver.hpp:184-187). A shared PMP/PMA helper is NOT warranted: the cfg arrays differ in packing/indexing (PMP is a 16-wide sparse array stepped `i += 2` reading `pmpcfg[i]`; PMA is a 2-wide packed array stepped `2*i` reading `pmacfg[i]`), so a unifying helper would add parameters without reducing complexity. Task already sanctions this mirroring.

- "read all CSRs in a list" helper (state_drain.hpp:115-125) — none exists; reuses `read_register_64` per entry, identical idiom to the existing mscratch/mepc/mcause re-reads above it. PMA loops mirror the same shape. Clean.

- `has_andes` detection (hybrid_handoff.c:315-329) — consistent, not duplicated. It follows the existing `has_fp` (lines 283-288) and `has_v`/`has_other_v` (lines 348-353) idiom exactly: a local int set to 1 on any non-NULL handle, then `|=` the flag. There is no `detect_feature()` helper for `has_fp`/`has_v` to reuse — they are inline too — so `has_andes` matching that inline form is the correct consistent choice, not a missed reuse.

- `find_reg`-by-index loops (hybrid_handoff.c:165-173) — the PMA `g_snprintf("pmacfg%d"/"pmaaddr%d") + find_reg` loops duplicate the shape of the existing PMP loops directly below (lines 174-181), but that is the existing inline convention (there is no indexed-resolve helper for PMP either) and the task explicitly sanctions mirroring PMP. Not worth extracting for 2 vs 4 loops.

Nothing to change.
